SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

revolution noun

the overthrow of a government

also revolutions, revolutionary, revolutionaries, uprising, plot a revolution

classical

Caes. BG 1.9.3: novīs rēbus studēbat
Cic. Cat. 1.3: novīs rēbus studentem (Lewis & Short, s.v. novus)
M-O s.v. revolutionary

rēs novae, rērum novārum f. pl.

plural noun phrase, “new things”

revolution, political upheaval

Political innovation, overthrow (Lewis & Short): to aim at revolution is novīs rēbus studēre; a revolutionary is rērum novārum cupidus (Cic., Sall.; M-O) or studiōsus. Out of context rēs novae can also be plain news or new things.

Other words

  • commūtātiō, commūtātiōnis f. — a change of constitution

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 1.65: dē commūtātiōnibus rērum pūblicārum; Cic. Fam. 5.12.4: cīvīlēs commūtātiōnēs (Lewis & Short)

    A change in general (of seasons, of fortune); with reī pūblicae or cīvīlis, a change of the state’s form, as from kingship to tyranny (Cic. Rep. 1).

  • conversiō, conversiōnis f. — an overturning, an upheaval

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 1.69: nōn est enim causa conversiōnis; Cic. Flacc. 94: conversiō et perturbātiō rērum (Lewis & Short)

    A turning round: properly the revolving of the heavens, then a political overturn (Lewis & Short).

  • revolūtiō, revolūtiōnis f. — a revolving

    noun, third declension · avoid · late Latin · Aug. Civ. 22.12 (Lewis & Short)

    Late Latin for conversiō, of turning in a circle (Lewis & Short); never of politics in ancient Latin.

Examples

  • cupiditāte rēgnī adductus novīs rēbus studēbat

    led on by desire for the throne, he was eager for revolutionCaes. BG 1.9.3

  • rērum novārum cupidī, victōrēs praesertim et armātī, vim et manūs adferent

    the men hungry for revolution, victorious as they are and armed, will lay violent hands on meCic. Att. 9.12.3

  • mīrīque sunt orbēs et quasi circumitūs in rēbus pūblicīs commūtātiōnum et vicissitūdinum

    and there are wonderful cycles, a kind of round, of changes and reversals in statesCic. Rep. 1.45

See also government, change, political.

SourcesLewis & Short: novus · Lewis & Short: commutatio · Lewis & Short: conversio · Lewis & Short: revolutio

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. revolutionary.
